newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French 10-year bond futures settled lower in modest volume on Thursday as the market consolidated after three consecutive sessions of gains, analysts said.
"The market has had a lot of upside events in recent sessions," said Merrill Lynch analyst Joanne Perez. "It's just consolidating."

Bond futures spent all of the day in negative territory, ending the session at 128.34, down 0.26 -- toward the bottom of their 32-point trading range -- after a weak opening by U.S. Treasuries gave no support.
Analysts said the Bank of France's decision to leave interest rates unchanged after its regular monetary policy council meeting was expected.

Still, analysts said, that did not rule out the possibility that disappointment at maintenance of the status quo might have hurt three-month PIBOR interest rate futures which ended three basis points lower at 96.65.
"There might have been some hope the BoF could have made a symbolic gesture and lowered the ceiling rate," said CCF economist Antoine Brunet.
The market ignored U.S. weekly jobless claims which totalled 318,000, a figure above the consensus forecast of 313,000.

Analysts said the market was waiting for Friday's U.S. retails sales and producer prices. "Very few people want to be long or short going into these figures. That's why volume is so modest," said one.
"People are very nervous about retail sales as it is known to be a figure that (U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan) Greenspan monitors closely," said Brunet.
Another analyst said the market had already built in expectations of another 25 basis point rise in the U.S. Fed funds rate "and that's why the market is more likely to respond to weak figures".
French March inflation figures were due at 0645 GMT on Friday.

The consensus forecast was for month-on-month growth of 0.3 percent, resulting in a year on year rise of 1.3 percent. The expected benign data would support the case for further Bank of France easing, economists said.
A modest drop last month in French consumer confidence shown by figures released on Thursday by national statistics institute INSEE had no market impact.
Economists said that the downturn in confidence was likely temporary, citing an overall improved economic outlook.
"Most likely, the March drop in consumer sentiment does not herald the start of a new deterioration," said Salomon Brothers' Jean-Francois Mercier.
INSEE's confidence indicator, which shows how much negative views outweigh positive ones in percentage points, slipped to -32 from -30.
Economists said renewed pessimism about the labour market, likely triggered by publicity over job cuts announced by French carmaker Renault, was a key factor behind the March drop in confidence.

But they said improving business sentiment should boost job growth in coming quarters. They added while fiscal policy was expected to remain restrictive, the government was unlikely to introduce new individual taxes or big cuts in welfare benefits ahead of the 1998 parliametnary elections.
The franc was steady at 3.3650 per mark, unchanged from the previous day.
-- Penny MacRae, Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
